fact_label: Territorial tax system — foreign-sourced income exempt
notes: Belize runs a territorial tax system: foreign-sourced income generally falls outside the scope of Belizean income tax for residents, and the Qualified Retired Persons (QRP) status carries an explicit permanent exemption on foreign-sourced income, capital gains, and estate tax on top of the baseline. Same favorable shape as Guatemala's territorial system (see GT:territorial-tax-system-foreign-sourced-income-exempt) and the opposite of Colombia's worldwide-income-once-resident model. This is the load-bearing fact behind the Income viability criterion's 4/5 score at Corozal and every other Belize location — genuinely national policy, not location-specific — extracted for the first time; the criterion previously had zero backing fact rows in this file despite real sourced reasoning already in our records and visa-legal.md. Cross-corroborated with greenbacktaxservices.com. Caveat carried from source: US citizens remain fully subject to US worldwide-income taxation regardless of Belize residency status — this exemption addresses Belizean tax exposure only, not a US filer's home-country obligation. No US-Belize double-taxation treaty was confirmed in this pass, flagged as a genuine open question in visa-legal.md

fact_label: No residency status required to open a Belizean bank account
notes: Non-resident foreigners can open accounts. Several Belizean banks work with non-resident foreign clients; document requirements (notarized passport copy, proof of address, bank reference letter with 2+ years' history, sometimes a reference from a Belizean citizen or permanent resident) vary by bank, and some banks permit fully remote account opening while others don't. Typical processing time 1-2 weeks once documents are in order. Reads as more open than Guatemala's or Colombia's residency-gated banking norms — a real, practical plus for the bootstrapping period before any residency status is settled, and the second of the two facts explicitly cited in the Income viability criterion's 4/5 score for Corozal/Belize generally (our records row 56). Cross-corroborated with worldvisaguide.com and belizerealestatesearch.com. National policy, not Corozal-specific, but applies identically to Corozal since it isn't gated by which Belize district an applicant plans to live in
